keyTakeaways: SurtitleLive is becoming Pockitle Cue; existing accounts, projects, and the prepared-surtitling browser workflow remain.
Pockitle Cue is for text prepared before a performance; Pockitle Live captions speech that happens in the moment.
Pockitle Cue for Mac and Pockitle Live for iOS are in development, so their described capabilities are not released features yet.
On iPhone and iPad, Pockitle Live Web can use only external audio inputs that iOS lists in the browser; the built-in microphone is the fallback when none is listed.

faq.question: What is changing from SurtitleLive to Pockitle Cue?
faq.answer: SurtitleLive is taking the name Pockitle Cue. Existing accounts, projects, and the core browser workflow for preparing, reviewing, rehearsing, and cueing surtitles remain.

faq.question: What is the difference between Pockitle Cue and Pockitle Live?
faq.answer: Pockitle Cue is for prepared text that can be reviewed and rehearsed before a performance. Pockitle Live creates captions from speech that is happening now.

faq.question: Are Pockitle Cue for Mac and Pockitle Live for iOS available now?
faq.answer: No. Both native apps are described as in development. Their planned projection and audio-input capabilities should not be treated as released features.

faq.question: Can Pockitle Live Web use an external microphone on iPhone or iPad?
faq.answer: Only when iOS exposes that microphone as an available browser audio input. A connected microphone or mixer route that does not appear in the list cannot be selected; the built-in microphone is the dependable fallback.

glossary.definition: The browser-based prepared-surtitling product formerly called SurtitleLive.
Text prepared, reviewed, and rehearsed before it is cued during a performance.
The browser-based tool for captioning speech that cannot be fully prepared in advance.
A Mac app in development for synced local projection and a closer QLab workflow.
An iPhone and iPad app in development for more direct access to supported external audio inputs.
